review_style.value: Doesn't read the code. AI reviewers, CI and preview gates merge low and medium risk; high risk waits for a human
review_style.quote: The intent is that you set up a system in which you do not need to read the code.

also.quote: I'm at the point where once I've made a decision on something I tell the agent to go and it sends it off to production autonomously
High waits for Kent unless he explicitly said to merge.
if I could only have one, then I would keep the the Cursor BugBot one because it seems to have caught more problems.
Man I haven't written a test all year
I didn't read that diff line by line. I read the outcome: does it do what we decided it should do, and did the gates I trust pass?
The agent wrote the implementation, tests, and PR. Automated gates and AI reviewers checked the work.
I have auto-fix enabled, so when BugBot finds issues, it automatically fires off an agent to fix the bug.

And so I typically like to have the review agent and the actual agent do a couple iterations. So build it out, test it nicely, and then have the agent review it, iterate on each one of these steps. And only when all that's done, then I'm going to go and review it with my time.

value: composed with Cursor Cloud agent hooks

signature.caption: auto-merges low and medium risk
signature.why: Our pick: a cloud agent ticks its own PR through AI reviewers and CI, picks a risk level, and merges everything below high unattended, so the diff goes unread.
signature.quote: - **Merge:** auto-merge low and medium once CI is green and valid reviewer

also.quote: Babysit a PR. Iterate with AI reviewers and CI. Get it ready and maybe merge. Send summary message.

archetype.why: Talks to Grok bots that run Cursor and Devin cloud agents shipping dozens of PRs a day; says the running count is no longer known.

signature_quote.value: Agents produce output. You own the outcome.
signature_quote.more: That's not a consolation prize. Owning the outcome was always the valuable part.
